questions.q: Per its own description on the New Flow screen, what launches a Platform Event-Triggered Flow?
options: A platform event message being received
A specified date and time
A record being created, updated, or deleted
A user clicking a quick action
questions.explain: Its description reads: "Launches when a platform event message is received. This autolaunched flow runs in the background."

questions.q: Like a scheduled flow or an Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger), what does a Platform Event-Triggered Flow have in common with them?
options: It always shows a screen to the user who triggers it
It cannot create or update records
It runs in the background with no screen
It can only be activated by a system administrator
questions.explain: All three are autolaunched-style flows that run in the background — what differs between them is only the trigger.

questions.q: What does a Platform Event-Triggered Flow's Start element ask you to configure?
options: A schedule and frequency
A screen layout
A referenced (child) flow
Which platform event to subscribe to
questions.explain: The Start element's only configuration is Choose Platform Event — picking which event this flow subscribes to.

questions.q: In this lesson's Pause element example, what does the flow do before resuming?
options: It waits for a Vendor Response platform event message confirming the order shipped
It waits for a scheduled time of day
It waits for a user to approve a screen
It waits for a Subflow element to finish
questions.explain: The flow submits an order, then pauses until a Vendor Response platform event message confirms it shipped, filtered by order number and status.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a Platform Event-Triggered Flow and a flow using a Pause element to wait for a platform event?
options: There is no difference — they are the same mechanism
A Platform Event-Triggered Flow is born from the event message at its Start; a Pause element lets any already-running flow stop and wait for one partway through
Pause elements can only be used in Screen Flows
Platform Event-Triggered Flows cannot use filter conditions on the event
questions.explain: The Start-element subscription launches a brand-new flow run from an event; a Pause element suspends an already-running flow until a matching event arrives.
